luke.5.p1.b1.text: On one occasion, while Jesus was standing by the Lake of Gennesaret with the crowd pressing in on Him to hear the word of God,

luke.5.p1.b2.text: He saw two boats at the edge of the lake. The fishermen had left them and were washing their nets.

luke.5.p1.b3.text: Jesus got into the boat belonging to Simon and asked him to put out a little from shore.

luke.5.p1.b4.text: And sitting down, He taught the people from the boat.

luke.5.p2.b1.text: “Put out into deep water and let down your nets for a catch.”

luke.5.p2.b2.text: “Master,” … “we have worked hard all night without catching anything.

luke.5.p2.b3.text: But because You say so, I will let down the nets.”

luke.5.p3.b1.text: When they had done so, they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to tear.

luke.5.p3.b2.text: So they signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them,

luke.5.p3.b3.text: and they came and filled both boats so full that they began to sink.

luke.5.p4.b1.text: When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus’ knees.

luke.5.p4.b2.text: “Go away from me, Lord,” … “for I am a sinful man.”

luke.5.p4.b3.text: For he and his companions were astonished at the catch of fish they had taken,

luke.5.p5.b1.text: and so were his partners James and John, the sons of Zebedee.

luke.5.p5.b2.text: “Do not be afraid,” … “From now on you will catch men.”

luke.5.p5.b3.text: And when they had brought their boats ashore, they left everything and followed Him.

luke.5.p6.b1.text: While Jesus was in one of the towns, a man came along who was covered with leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he fell facedown

luke.5.p6.b2.text: “Lord, if You are willing, You can make me clean.”

luke.5.p6.b4.text: “Do not tell anyone,” … “But go, show yourself to the priest …

luke.5.p7.b1.text: But the news about Jesus spread all the more,

luke.5.p7.b2.text: and great crowds came to hear Him and to be healed of their sicknesses.

luke.5.p7.b3.text: Yet He frequently withdrew to the wilderness to pray.

luke.5.p8.b1.text: One day Jesus was teaching, and the Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there. People had come from Jerusalem and from every village of Galilee and Judea,

luke.5.p8.b2.text: and the power of the Lord was present for Him to heal the sick.

luke.5.p8.b3.text: Just then some men came carrying a paralyzed man on a mat. They tried to bring him inside to set him before Jesus,

luke.5.p8.b4.text: but they could not find a way through the crowd. So they went up on the roof

luke.5.p9.b1.text: and lowered him on his mat through the tiles into the middle of the crowd, right in front of Jesus.

luke.5.p9.b2.text: When Jesus saw their faith, He said,

luke.5.p10.b1.text: “Who is this man who speaks blasphemy? Who can forgive sins but God alone?”

luke.5.p10.b2.text: “I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”

luke.5.p10.b3.text: And immediately the man stood up before them, took what he had been lying on, and went home glorifying God.

luke.5.p11.b1.text: After this, Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth.

luke.5.p11.b3.text: and Levi got up, left everything, and followed Him.

luke.5.p12.b1.text: Then Levi hosted a great banquet for Jesus at his house. A large crowd of tax collectors was there, along with others who were eating with them.

luke.5.p12.b2.text: “Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”

luke.5.p12.b3.text: “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.

luke.5.p12.b4.text: I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance.”

luke.5.p13.b1.text: “John’s disciples and those of the Pharisees frequently fast and pray, but Yours keep on eating and drinking.”

luke.5.p13.b2.text: “Can you make the guests of the bridegroom fast while He is with them?

luke.5.p13.b3.text: But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.”

luke.5.p14.b1.text: “No one tears a piece of cloth from a new garment and sews it on an old one. If he does, he will tear the new garment as well,

luke.5.p14.b2.text: And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the new wine will burst the skins, the wine will spill,

luke.5.p14.b3.text: Instead, new wine is poured into new wineskins.

luke.5.p14.b4.text: And no one after drinking old wine wants new, for he says, ‘The old is better.’”
